Ithiel
ITH-i-el
n. (proper, one addressed by Agur; also a Benjamite)
Hebrew Iythiyel, commonly read as God is with me. The name appears twice: in a Benjamite pedigree in Nehemiah, and at the head of the last-but-one chapter of Proverbs, as one of the two men Agur spake unto.

Biblical Definition

The Benjamite appears in the list of those who dwelt at Jerusalem after the return: “And these are the sons of Benjamin; Sallu the son of Meshullam, the son of Joed, the son of Pedaiah, the son of Kolaiah, the son of Maaseiah, the son of Ithiel, the son of Jesaiah” (Nehemiah 11:7). The famous occurrence opens Proverbs 30: “The words of Agur the son of Jakeh, even the prophecy: the man spake unto Ithiel, even unto Ithiel and Ucal” (Proverbs 30:1). Nothing more is told of either hearer. What follows is one of the most remarkable passages in the wisdom books: a man who confesses himself more brutish than any man and without the understanding of a man, who asks What is his name, and what is his son's name, if thou canst tell?, who declares every word of God pure and warns against adding to his words, and who prays to be given neither poverty nor riches.

Origin & Era

Webster (1828) has no entry for this proper name; Scripture fixes it as one of the two men to whom Agur the son of Jakeh spake his prophecy, and as a Benjamite in Nehemiah 11.

expand to see more

PROPHECY, n. A foretelling; prediction; a declaration of something to come; in Scripture, also a burden or oracle.

BRUTISH, a. Resembling a brute or beast; insensible; stupid; unfeeling; ignorant.

PURE, a. Separate from all heterogeneous or extraneous matter; clear; unmingled; free from moral defilement.

AGUR, n. The son of Jakeh, the author of the thirtieth chapter of Proverbs.

CONVENIENT, a. Fit; suitable; proper; adapted to use or to wants; as, food convenient for me.

Key Scripture

Proverbs 30:1 — "The words of Agur the son of Jakeh, even the prophecy: the man spake unto Ithiel, even unto Ithiel and Ucal,"

Nehemiah 11:7 — "And these are the sons of Benjamin; Sallu the son of Meshullam, the son of Joed, the son of Pedaiah, the son of Kolaiah, the son of Maaseiah, the son of Ithiel, the son of Jesaiah."

Proverbs 30:5 — "Every word of God is pure: he is a shield unto them that put their trust in him."

Proverbs 30:8 — "Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me:"

Modern Corruption

Confidence is the currency of modern teaching, and the chapter addressed to Ithiel opens with a teacher confessing he is more brutish than any man — and then speaks with more authority than any confident man could.

expand to see more

Proverbs 30 is addressed to Ithiel and Ucal, and it begins where almost no modern instruction would dare: Surely I am more brutish than any man, and have not the understanding of a man. I neither learned wisdom, nor have the knowledge of the holy. Then a series of questions no man can answer — who hath ascended up into heaven, or descended? who hath gathered the wind in his fists? who hath bound the waters in a garment? — and at the end, What is his name, and what is his son's name, if thou canst tell? The teacher establishes his authority by confessing the limit of his knowledge, which is the opposite of how authority is usually claimed.

What he is certain about is the word: Every word of God is pure: he is a shield unto them that put their trust in him. Add thou not unto his words, lest he reprove thee, and thou be found a liar. And what he asks for is moderation: neither poverty nor riches, lest he be full and deny God, or poor and steal and take the name of his God in vain. A man who knows how little he knows, who will not add a syllable to Scripture, and who fears prosperity as much as want — that is the teacher Ithiel got, and the church could use more of them.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Iythiyel (H384), God is with me; Aguwr (H94), gathered; massa (H4853), a burden or oracle; tsaraph (H6884), to refine or try.

expand to see more

Hebrew Iythiyel (H384) — Ithiel; commonly read as God is with me.

Hebrew Aguwr (H94) — Agur, gathered; the son of Jakeh who spake this prophecy.

Hebrew massa (H4853) — a burden, an oracle; the AV's even the prophecy.

Hebrew tsaraph (H6884) — to smelt, to refine; every word of God is pure, that is, tried.

Hebrew choq (H2706) — an appointed portion; feed me with food convenient for me.

Usage

"“The man spake unto Ithiel, even unto Ithiel and Ucal”."

"“Every word of God is pure: he is a shield unto them that put their trust in him”."

"“Give me neither poverty nor riches” — what the teacher prayed for."
